lessonRef.subject: mathematics
lessonRef.title: Concept model A: reading and writing numerical expressions

sections.title: Instructional examples
sections.directions: Study both examples. The second one drops some of the wording of the first.

items.prompt: Describe 5 × (12 + 3) in words without evaluating it.

steps: The parentheses show that 12 and 3 are added first.
workedSolution.answer: Add 12 and 3, then multiply the sum by 5.

items.prompt: Let E represent 18 + 7. Without evaluating, compare 4 × (18 + 7) with E.

steps: The parentheses contain the same expression represented by E.
The factor 4 multiplies that entire expression, so the new expression is 4 times E.

sections.title: Guided practice
sections.directions: Work these with your teaching parent. Say the reason for each step out loud before you write it.

items.prompt: A supply cart has 3 boxes with 10 markers in each box and 6 loose markers. Which expression represents the total number of markers?
A garden has 5 trays with 9 seedlings in each tray and 15 extra seedlings. How many seedlings are there in all?
In 193326, how does the value of the 3 in the thousands place compare with the value of the 3 in the hundreds place?

sections.title: Independent practice
sections.directions: Work on your own. Show the steps that produced each answer.

items.prompt: Round each number to the nearest ten to estimate 366 + 797.
Round 418 to the nearest hundred and 84 to the nearest ten, then multiply to estimate the product.
A student says 8585 - 1108 = 7577. Round each number to the nearest hundred. Which choice correctly checks the claim?
choices: The claim is not exact; the exact result is 7477 and the rounded estimate is 7500.
The claim is exact; the rounded estimate is 7600.
The claim is not exact; the exact result is 7577 and the rounded estimate is 7500.
The claim is not exact; the exact result is 7477 and the rounded estimate is 7600.

items.prompt: A student evaluates 4 × [21 + (11 - 4)] + 19: “They multiply 4 by 21 first, then finish the calculation, so the value is 110.” Which statement best identifies the error?
choices: The student used the right first step but made an arithmetic slip; the value should be 133.
The grouping symbols do not affect the order; 110 is the value.
The student multiplied before evaluating (11 - 4); the innermost difference is 7, giving 131.
The first error is in the final addition or subtraction; the value should be 132.

sections.title: Mastery check
sections.directions: Mastery check. Work without help, then stop and hand this section in.

items.prompt: A student says, “In 975446, the value of the 4 in the hundreds place is 1/10 as much as the value of the 4 in the tens place.” Which statement best analyzes the error?
choices: The values are 400 and 40; 400 is 10 times as much as 40, so the student's comparison is incorrect.
The places are adjacent, so 400 is 100 times as much as 40.
The values are 400 and 40; 400 is 1/10 as much as 40, so the student's comparison is correct.
The values are 400 and 40; 400 is 1/10 as much as 40.
